text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Andris Shkele goes on a one-day private visit to Lithuania to meet Lithuanian counterpart Gediminas Vagnorius. The sea border issue between Lithuania and Latvia will be one, but not the only topic, he is going to discuss.
- The Latvian border guard commander said the force needs around 1.5 million lats of additional funding to be made entirely professional and to stop being manned by conscripts.

- The head of the state medical fund said delayed salaries will be paid out to medical personnel next week. She noted the delay is due to the introduction of a new funding scheme for medical institutions.

- Latvia's Energy Agency has worked out a plan to explore for oil and to develop the oil industry. The resources in both Latvia's continental shelf and on land are estimated at between 35 to 52 million tonnes and worth $15 billion in prices expected to be current from 2000.

- The privatisation agency plans privatisation vouchers worth 700 million lats to be paid off this year. The agency expects to sell the shares of 29 state companies in public offers. The main task will be selling the shares of major companies with a more than 50 percent state stake.
- The Bank of Latvia announced it will keep reducing its rates of discount. From today the refinancing rate is reduced to nine percent a year from 9.5 percent.

- Representatives of Latvia's five largest Russian-language papers call for support for a nation-wide referendum on ending voting restrictions for non-citizens, mostly Russian-speakers, in the local elections.

- Privatisation agency director Janis Naglis said foreign investors will only be allowed to buy new shares in Ventspils Nafta oil terminal, possibly by taking part in construction projects related to the company's development.
